validator_locations.combat_tags_and_jutsu_item: app/src/validators/combat.ts (AllTags union at :872, 76 members; JutsuValidatorRawSchema at :1290s; ItemValidatorRawSchema at :1435)

unknown_key_rule.claim: THE GENERALIZED SILENT-FAILURE RULE. Across all of app/src/validators/*.ts and app/drizzle/schema.ts, .strict() appears exactly once, on an unrelated travel validator. Neither passthrough() nor strip() appears at all. Every content entity validator is therefore non-strict, and Zod's default applies: an unknown or misspelled key is DROPPED at .input() parse time, with no error, and the mutation proceeds and reports success.
unknown_key_rule.note: Where the stripping happens: Zod's own object parse inside each procedure's .input(), not a bespoke function. There is no single file to point at, which is precisely why the failure is invisible. Corollary for a client: the only place an unknown key can ever raise an error is client-side, before the send.

empty_string_rule.claim: Content mutations run setEmptyStringsToNulls(input.data, <table>) before writing. Any key whose value is exactly '' becomes null, EXCEPT where the Drizzle column is notNull (typeutils.ts:66, 'if (columns?.[propertyKey]?.notNull) continue').
empty_string_rule.note: Table-aware, so the same empty string is nulled on one entity and preserved on another. Call sites include profile.ts:1497, badge.ts:64, bloodline.ts:649.

coercion_rule.claim: Numeric and boolean fields are overwhelmingly z.coerce.*, so a string '5' becomes 5 and a truthy value becomes true rather than erroring. Zod 4 (^4.4.3) is in use, which is why .prefault() rather than .default() appears throughout.

cross_field_rule.claim: Constraints that no single field expresses live in three superRefine functions: SuperRefineEffects (all entities, :1235), SuperRefineJutsu (:1207) and SuperRefineItem (:1122). These produce a 400 on a payload that is shape-valid, and they are invisible to any field-by-field schema view.
cross_field_rule.match: export const SuperRefineEffects = (effects: ZodAllTags[], ctx: z.RefinementCtx) => {
cross_field_rule.note: Examples read directly: wound/vamp/consume each require a damage or pierce effect in the same effects array (:1238-1258); activatesagemode is rejected on every entity (:1263) and again by name in the jutsu (:1214) and item (:1130) refinements; powerPerLevel must be 0 for rollbloodline, rollsagemode, removebloodline and noncombatconsumereward (:1259-1271).

error_vs_coerce_vs_strip.claim: For any field on a content entity, the outcome of a bad value is one of three, and which one is structural rather than per-field: an UNKNOWN key is stripped silently (unknown_key_rule); a KNOWN key with a coercible wrong type is coerced (coercion_rule); a KNOWN key with a value outside its enum, bound or cross-field constraint errors with data.zodError populated (transport.error_envelope). Empty string is a fourth case, converted to null or preserved by column nullability (empty_string_rule).
error_vs_coerce_vs_strip.population_scanned: Derived from the four anchored rules above it in this section (unknown_key_rule, coercion_rule, empty_string_rule, cross_field_rule), each with its own anchor. No additional scan; this entry is the synthesis, not a separate claim.
error_vs_coerce_vs_strip.note: This four-way rule is the actionable generalization the dispatch asked for. Only the first case is silent, and only the first case is fully preventable client-side.

mutation_return.claim: A content create returns baseServerResponse and puts the NEW ID IN THE MESSAGE FIELD. It does not return the persisted record. jutsu.create does the same.
mutation_return.note: message is overloaded: on success it carries an id, on failure a human sentence. Any client must read message positionally by outcome, not as display text.

id_generation.claim: Ids are minted server-side with nanoid() at create time (also asset.ts:177, :221 and jutsu.ts:16). Default nanoid length is 21 characters, which matches the ID_LEN = 21 constant tnr-tools already validates against.
id_generation.note: An id is first knowable to a client from the create response message. There is no client-side id reservation path in source.

create_inserts_placeholder.claim: create does not accept a payload. It inserts a fixed placeholder row (gameAsset: name 'Placeholder', type 'STATIC', image and url IMG_AVATAR_DEFAULT) and returns its id. jutsu.create inserts name `New Jutsu - ${id}`.
create_inserts_placeholder.note: Consequence worth recording: the 'blank shell named New Jutsu - <id>' that tnr-tools treats as a corruption symptom is simply what create always produces. The shell is visible whenever the follow-up update does not land, so create-then-fill is inherently two-phase and the intermediate state is a real, reachable record.

read_back_ground_truth.claim: Per entity the read-back procedure is a query taking z.object({id: z.string()}): gameAsset.get (asset.ts:147), jutsu.get (jutsu.ts:266), item.get (item.ts:197), quests.get (quests.ts:215), bloodline.get (bloodline.ts:133), profile.getAi (profile.ts:1121, input z.object({userId})).
read_back_ground_truth.note: Shape asymmetry: create accepts no payload at all, update accepts a validator-shaped data object, and get returns the DB row. So the read-back shape matches neither input shape.

hidden_and_publish.claim: hidden exists as a column on content tables and is part of the update payload, but no dedicated publish or visibility-toggle procedure exists for jutsu, item, quest, bloodline or gameAsset.

tag_power_max_is_wrong.claim: 45g.tag_power_max asserts a maximum of 100 for essentially every tag, including damage, heal, absorb, increasedamagegiven, decreasedamagetaken and decreasestat. In source those tags are UNCAPPED: PowerAttributes.power is z.coerce.number().min(0) with no max (app/src/validators/combat.ts:111) and is spread AFTER BaseAttributes in all 61 tags that use it (e.g. combat.ts:164-167), overriding the capped BaseAttributes.power at combat.ts:98.
tag_power_max_is_wrong.note: THIS IS A GENERATOR DEFECT, not merely staleness. schema_extract.py appears to read the first power declaration it sees and not account for a later spread overriding it. The consequence propagates: 45g.tag_power_max feeds validate.py:769-770, which errors on any power > 100 and so rejects payloads the server would accept. Re-pointing the generator at a newer SHA will not fix this; the extraction logic must handle spread precedence.

findings.claim: No Access-Control-Allow-* header is set anywhere, and no CORS middleware or Next headers() entry configures one. G5_rate_limits.answer: 60 requests per 60 seconds sliding window, keyed per procedure path plus identity, on publicProcedure only; violations by logged-in users cost 1 percent of money and bank.

findings.claim: Upstash sliding window, 60 per 60s, prefix 'trpc-ratelimit', analytics on.
The limiter key is procedure path plus userId, falling back to IP for anonymous callers. So the budget is per procedure, not global: a client spreading work across many procedures gets 60 each.
On a trip, a logged-in caller has movedTooFastCount incremented and money and bank each multiplied by 0.99, before a TOO_MANY_REQUESTS error is thrown.
findings.note: The thrown message is 'You are acting too fast. Incident logged for review on path {path}. 1% money reduced.' (trpc.ts:177). This is a real financial penalty on a real account, which is why the scope question below matters.

findings.claim: SCOPE: publicProcedure applies ratelimitMiddleware. protectedProcedure (trpc.ts:213) does not. Every content procedure a builder calls is protectedProcedure.
findings.note: Population for the negative half: all 58 files in app/src/server/api/routers scanned; ratelimitMiddleware appears outside trpc.ts only at misc.ts:108 and towerDefense.ts:116 and :157, each hand-composed with hasUserMiddleware. 651 protectedProcedure occurrences against 122 publicProcedure.

findings.claim: If Redis is unreachable the limiter fails OPEN in development and CLOSED in production.
The MCP surface is stricter and doubly limited: 30 per 60s by IP pre-auth (prefix mcp-ratelimit) and 30 per 60s per user post-auth (prefix mcp-user-ratelimit, route.ts:33).
Nothing in source treats batching as abusive per se; the limiter counts requests by procedure path and identity, and a batch is one HTTP request carrying several calls.
findings.population_scanned: Population: trpc.ts read in full; grep across app/src for batch, abuse, throttle, suspicious. Whether an edge layer in front of Next counts batches differently is outside this repo.

G6_client_visibility.answer: A browser-only gate exists in source and is commented out. User-agent is captured and logged but gates nothing on the content path. Reported factually; no conclusion about permission is drawn here.

findings.claim: A uaMiddleware that would return HTTP 403 with the message 'Forbidden. Only access through browser' for any user-agent whose parsed browser name is undefined is present in source, fully written, and COMMENTED OUT (proxy.ts:11-21). Its call site is also commented out at proxy.ts:101-102, '// Ensure valid user agent' / '// return uaMiddleware(request);'.
findings.note: This is the most directly relevant item in the audit for G6 and it cuts both ways: the capability was built and is currently disabled. Whether a native client is sanctioned is not a source question and is explicitly out of this audit's remit.

findings.claim: A crawler regex exists and is live, but it only pins an A/B layout variant and only when pathname is '/' (proxy.ts:70 returns early otherwise). It blocks nothing and never touches /api/trpc.
user-agent is read into every tRPC context.
No content procedure branches on userAgent. Every use found is a write into a log or report row, truncated to 180 characters.
findings.population_scanned: Population: grep for userAgent across all of app/src, 8 non-MCP hits. Uses are misc.ts:76 and :90-92, profile.ts:335-337 and :1117 (logging), utils/hardware.ts:9-12 (client-side device string parsing), proxy.ts:57 (the crawler A/B pin above). No hit is a gate on a content mutation.

findings.claim: No bot-detection service, device-attestation, headless-browser check or fingerprinting library is wired into the request path.
findings.population_scanned: Population: app/package.json dependency list read in full; grep across app/src for recaptcha, turnstile, hcaptcha, fingerprint, botd, datadome, arcjet, headless, webdriver.

findings.claim: The game repo contains CLAUDE.md, CODEOWNERS, CONTRIBUTING.md, DEVELOPMENT.md and README.md at root. Their contents were NOT read in this pass, deliberately: the dispatch reserves the permission question for dauntless and the admin, so summarising policy prose here would overstep and would risk reproducing repo text.
findings.note: Flagged so the gap is visible rather than silent. If a policy read is wanted it should be a separate, explicitly scoped request.

G7_webview_viability.answer: Nothing in the auth path, redirects or CSP is expressed in source that is known to break inside an Android WebView; this is INFERRED from absence and is the weakest answer in this section.

findings.claim: No Content-Security-Policy is set in this repo.
findings.population_scanned: Population: app/next.config.mjs read; grep across app/src and next.config.mjs for Content-Security-Policy, contentSecurityPolicy, frame-ancestors, X-Frame-Options. No hits.

findings.claim: The only redirect-shaped logic in the proxy is the landing-page A/B rewrite on '/' and an early return for MCP routes. The tRPC path receives neither.

Clerk's hosted sign-in flow, third-party cookie behaviour and any FAPI redirect are library and configuration concerns not expressed in this repo, so WebView compatibility cannot be settled from source. The proxy does keep Clerk's optional frontend API proxy path compatible (proxy.ts:181, '/__clerk/(.*)'), which is the one source-visible hint that a same-origin auth path is available.
findings.population_scanned: Population: app/src/proxy.ts (184 lines) read in full, app/package.json Clerk entries read, grep for __clerk, frontendApi, satellite, isSatellite across app/src.

redesign_spec.requirement: Speak superjson on both encode and decode, rather than hand-building meta envelopes.
redesign_spec.rationale: transport.transformer. Removes the entire class of per-field date and null coercion tables (D1) and is prerequisite to trusting any decoded response field.

redesign_spec.requirement: Read outcome from the decoded baseServerResponse: success as the verdict, message as the id carrier on create and as a sentence on failure. Never infer outcome from HTTP status.
redesign_spec.rationale: write_semantics.mutation_return and auth.role_miss_shape. A role miss is HTTP 200.

redesign_spec.requirement: Validate every outgoing payload against the entity's schema before sending, refusing unknown keys locally.
redesign_spec.rationale: divergence D4. Zod strips unknown keys silently server-side, so a pre-send refusal is the only place the error can surface at all.

redesign_spec.requirement: Derive that schema from a generator whose extraction handles spread precedence, and pin its output to a game commit SHA.
redesign_spec.rationale: fidelity.tag_power_max_is_wrong and the two provenance findings. R3 is only as good as its schema source, and the current one is provably wrong about power bounds.

redesign_spec.requirement: Treat create as a two-phase operation with a reachable intermediate state: create returns an id for a placeholder row, and the record is not correct until the follow-up update lands.
redesign_spec.rationale: write_semantics.create_inserts_placeholder. The intermediate row is visible to the game, so a client must be able to resume or report it, not just retry blindly.

redesign_spec.requirement: Read back through the entity's get query and diff against the keys actually asserted, not against the whole record.
redesign_spec.rationale: write_semantics.read_back_ground_truth. The get shape matches neither the create nor the update shape, so a whole-record diff produces noise.

redesign_spec.requirement: Budget requests per procedure path plus identity, not globally, and treat a limit trip as costly rather than as a retry signal.
redesign_spec.rationale: gates.G5. The key is `${path}-${userId}`, and a trip debits 1 percent of money and bank. Backoff is the wrong response to a penalty; not tripping it is the requirement.

redesign_spec.requirement: Carry the upload slug and its ceiling as data, not as a constant, since ceilings differ per slug (512KB, 256KB, 64KB).
Record, per procedure the client needs, whether it is reachable over the MCP surface, and treat that as a capability boundary rather than an implementation detail.
redesign_spec.rationale: procedures.mcp_boundary. Of the 26 procedures the current client calls, 14 are MCP-enabled and 12 are not, and the 12 include every jutsu, item and asset write plus the AI rules push. Any design that assumes a uniform surface is wrong in one direction or the other.

redesign_spec.requirement: Surface structured validation failures from data.zodError rather than parsing message strings.

by_dispatch: Balance data of any kind: drop rates, reward values, stat tuning, difficulty gates.
Any live request to theninja-rpg.com. No request was made, no credential was used, requested or synthesised.
Any modification to the game source, or a PR against it.
Any fix to builder_bundle.js, docs/, ENGINE_LAWS.md, skills/ or any manifest. This dispatch reports only.
Game prose. No dialog, item description or flavour text was extracted.
Any conclusion about whether a non-browser client is permitted.
deliberately_not_read: The game repo's CLAUDE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, DEVELOPMENT.md, README.md and CODEOWNERS. Recorded under G6 as a visible gap rather than summarised, because the permission question is reserved and summarising policy prose would overstep.
Per-field enumeration of every content entity field. See entities.scope_statement.
The 51 non-content routers, beyond counting procedure classes for the rate-limit population.
app/tests, except where a test name settled a behavioural question.

sequence: Cloned the game source shallow and pinned the SHA before reading anything.
Walked the tRPC core (trpc.ts, root.ts) and the front door (proxy.ts) in full.
Built the 167-procedure inventory and the entity validator map before opening builder_bundle.js.
Only then read builder_bundle.js and the generated data files, and diffed.
audit_method.self_correction: One extraction error was caught and fixed mid-audit: a fixed 26-line lookahead classified several .query() procedures as mutations by catching the next procedure's .mutation(. gameAsset.get, profile.getAi, jutsu.get, item.get, quests.get and bloodline.get were each verified individually as queries, and the inventory was rebuilt with proper procedure boundaries before any of it was used.
